provenance.mapping_decision: Problem 119 is a strengthened successor to frozen problem 104, not a retroactive replacement in the frozen snapshot. Problem 104 reconstructs one fixed single-wire cut and publishes its nine-component allocation rule. Problem 119 instead synthesizes a capacity-constrained multi-fragment plan and one shared robust allocation for hidden interaction graphs, observable lightcones, coherent calibration scenarios, and execution strata. It scores a planning artifact and an explicitly bounded variance proxy; it does not claim to execute or reconstruct all cut subexperiments.

title: Robust observable-lightcone cut-plan and shot-allocation synthesis
difficulty_explanation: Every seeded case is a 76-qubit three-matching circuit with 113 hidden RPP interactions, eighteen local Pauli observables, three coherent calibration scenarios, nine shared execution strata, and 2,415 feasible contiguous seven-fragment layouts. A full dense state is infeasible in the stated resource envelope. A submission must derive exact backward lightcones, obtain all 54 continuous pilot expectations through TensorCircuit, synthesize a capacity-feasible partition, identify every relevant cut by opaque ID, and find one shared integer allocation below a worst-target threshold. The 158-line expert sits close to the contract ceiling and gains leverage from exact causal-cone simulation plus compact deterministic resource synthesis rather than a prompt-exposed answer recipe.
solution_explanation: The constructive expert exploits exact at-most-eight-qubit observable cones for TensorCircuit pilots, then jointly searches capacity-feasible layouts and a threshold-feasible shared allocation using the declared independent-RPP variance proxy. The solver instruction does not disclose its allocation construction.
verification_explanation: The evaluator never imports TensorCircuit. It independently constructs complex128 NumPy causal-cone states from direct RPP matrices, compares that oracle against full dense eight-qubit circuits, exhaustively checks every feasible interval composition, recomputes cut/lightcone identities and variance certificates, and rejects strict type, contiguity, identity, finite-value, allocation, and certificate mutations.
relevant_experience: The reserve combines shallow-circuit causal cones, angle-dependent gate-cut QPD overhead, hardware-layout segmentation, coherent scenario robustness, shared-stratum sampling design under a worst-target objective, and exact artifact certification.

contract.determinism_scope: Exact cases are bound by the pinned image/runtime and evaluator-emitted full case_digest; an integer seed alone is not a cross-NumPy case identity.
contract.case_seed_source: verifier-only ORBIT_Q_CANDIDATE_SEED or evaluator --seed for local canaries
contract.hidden_holdout_status: pending; all listed host seeds are contaminated non-binding development canaries and no private holdout has been frozen or authorized
contract.anti_hardcoding: The seed changes the opaque qubit layout, 113 opaque interaction IDs, every RPP axis and angle, local rotations, eighteen observable identities/sites/Paulis, three calibration scenarios, nine execution-stratum identities and mixtures, excess-variance tables, fragment IDs, reference-selected interval sizes, active cuts, pilot values, and case digest.
contract.oracle: Independent complex128 NumPy causal-cone statevectors, a separate full dense eight-qubit lightcone canary, exhaustive layout enumeration, and independent artifact/variance recomputation

seed_protocol.base_seed_mapping: One NumPy Generator stream emits one 76-qubit case. Generation retries deterministically unless the reference joint plan is separated by at least 2.5 percent from both the balanced-layout reference allocation and the best of all 2,415 partitions under uniform shots.
seed_protocol.determinism_scope: Exact public case bytes are deterministic only under the bound runtime and are identified by the full evaluator-emitted case_digest.
seed_protocol.case_identity: SHA-256 of canonical JSON with sorted keys, compact separators, and allow_nan false over the exact public config before case_digest is inserted; stdout emits protocol_seed and full digest in exactly one orbit_q_case_identity JSON record.
seed_protocol.seed_scrub: The evaluator removes ORBIT_Q_CANDIDATE_SEED and all parsed evaluator CLI arguments before importing or invoking the submission.
seed_protocol.pinned_numpy_note: The target image pins NumPy 2.2.6. Trial manifests must bind full case_digest and image/runtime; local host digests are not authorized trial records.

difficulty_levers: a 76-qubit full state is dense-infeasible while each exact backward cone contains at most eight qubits
eighteen observables under three coherent scenarios require 54 quantum pilots and different active-cut subsets
2,415 capacity-feasible interval partitions interact nonlinearly with angle-dependent products of QPD factors
nine integer shot counts are shared by all 54 targets under a robust max objective rather than optimized independently
opaque shuffled identities and exact fragment, cut, lightcone, allocation, variance, and overhead artifacts prevent positional or certificate-only answers
the balanced-layout reference allocation and every partition paired with uniform shots are rejected by a generator-enforced positive gap on every admitted case
the 160-line ceiling forces a compact representation and coupled optimizer rather than separate hand-coded scenario solutions
claim_boundary: This is a deterministic synthetic pre-execution planning diagnostic. Its objective is an explicitly declared robust stratified variance proxy: independent per-RPP QPD factors are multiplied only on an observable's exact backward lightcone, and scenario-supplied excess variances are calibrated inputs. It neither reconstructs a cut expectation from real samples nor establishes actual hardware MSE, latency, optimal joint multi-gate QPD overhead, or a globally optimal integer allocation. The interval-layout restriction is part of the benchmark, not a claim about arbitrary graph partitioning. The evaluator uses an uncertified threshold reference and accepts any better feasible plan. Local NumPy validation establishes mathematical self-consistency only. The TensorCircuit expert has not run in the pinned image, Harbor has not run, no canonical task changed, no solver-model trial ran, and no model-hardness claim is made.

local_static_validation.binding_status: non-binding local design canaries only; no listed digest is authorized for a solver trial
local_static_validation.host_self_test_runtime_scope: one current-code default-seed solo run plus a concurrent four-seed rerun after exhaustive best-uniform gating; descriptive local evidence, not a pinned-runtime claim
local_static_validation.expert_proxy_scope: in-memory dense Circuit shim checking the expert's gate order, basis changes, expectation semantics, partition search, and certificates; not TensorCircuit execution or a pinned runtime estimate

admission_blockers: Candidate 119 intentionally has no entry in the frozen candidates.jsonl/shortlist and now has an exact-byte post-snapshot design_only registry binding. The safe runner rejects that lifecycle before both expert and model paths; only a future separately hashed, human-reviewed executable-promotion contract may authorize a run. Do not append or remap it into the frozen 1,000-contract snapshot.

After human design review, create and approve a separately hashed executable-promotion contract before any pinned run. Only then run the expert through the safe one-candidate workflow and verify XX/YY basis conjugations, cnot/rz RPP orientation, expectation_ps Pauli ordering, complex128 parity, runtime below the 180-second expert target, and peak memory.

After executable promotion, replace development digests with at least 25 exact pinned expert-only prequalification records, including protocol seed, case digest, pilot parity, selected fragments, cut/lightcone identities, allocation, baseline gaps, runtime, memory, and admission status.

Independently review whether multiplying single-gate RPP QPD factors is an acceptable benchmark proxy given that joint multi-gate decompositions can have lower overhead; do not relabel the proxy as optimal physical sampling cost.

Replace or independently certify the shared 96-step allocation heuristic before making any integer-minimax claim. A local one-shot exchange audit improved the default reference by 1.866 percent; the present contract is only threshold-feasible and deliberately accepts better allocations.

Audit whether exact enumeration of 2,415 layouts plus a fully specified max-target formula is still too recipe-exposed for a GPT-5.6 pilot. A pinned expert pass would establish feasibility, not likely model hardness.
Freeze verifier-only holdouts only after human review and complete authenticated expert functional, static-policy, and LLM-policy audits before any solver schedule.

Human reviewers must sign the RPP convention, backward-lightcone rule, independent-QPD product, stratum variance interpretation, layout restriction, integer allocation objective, tolerance policy, and post-snapshot provenance.
exploitability_risks: The feasible layout family is finite and the complete objective is public; a strong solver can enumerate partitions if it also implements the quantum pilots and robust allocation compactly enough.
Functional checks prove the returned artifact and metrics, but cannot prove that TensorCircuit rather than an unreported standalone cone simulator produced the pilots; source audit remains necessary.
The threshold is derived from the same deterministic case generator. Published evaluator, expert, and host seeds are contaminated development evidence and cannot establish private model hardness.
The output includes exact pilot expectations, so tolerance and source policy must reject hard-coded or externally sourced values without making valid TensorCircuit implementations brittle.
numerical_statistical_risks: QPD products amplify small pilot and angle differences; pinned-image parity is required before relying on the selected plan near its 0.8-percent threshold slack.
The deterministic excess-variance table is a planning calibration, not observed statistical uncertainty and not a confidence interval.

The reference allocation is an uncertified 96-step heuristic with integer rounding. A local one-shot exchange audit improved the default reference from 6.995601480311e-5 to 6.867465835582e-5; this does not break feasibility scoring, but it blocks any minimax-optimality claim.
NumPy Generator bytes can drift across versions, so exact case_digest and pinned NumPy are mandatory trial identity.
api_risks: The cnot-rz-cnot implementation must match exp(-i theta PP/2) after the XX and YY basis changes.
Circuit.expectation_ps must use integer Pauli codes 0=I, 1=X, 2=Y, 3=Z in the same qubit order as the independent oracle.
TensorCircuit backend and dtype settings are process global; complex128 is required for strict pilot parity.
The real TensorCircuit runtime for 54 separately constructed causal-cone circuits plus 2,415 allocation searches is unmeasured.
